No test is visible for the layouts.
Text sizing is estimated, so the result may differ from a real renderer.

terms.meaning: A list of positioned items that make up one slide.
A print unit used for font sizes. It is converted to screen pixels.
Gives the same output every time for the same input.
The summary of findings that drives the narrative slides.
Supporting pages placed at the back of the deck.
A colour written as a hash sign followed by six or three hexadecimal digits.

depends_on: lib/api-client-react/src/scan-deck.ts (likely source of the slide and element types; the import is not shown in the reviewed code).
used_by: Other tools that build decks in the same style, such as Lessons Learnt, through sceneKit (named in a code comment).

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Shared setup and drawing rules
sections.what: Sets the slide size, the template identifier, and the imports. The header comment lists the drawing rules that the editor and exporter must both follow, such as point sizes, text alignment, and how lines and colours are described.
sections.why: Likely reason: so the web editor and the PowerPoint exporter draw the same slide the same way.
sections.watch_out: If a renderer ignores these rules, its output will drift from the exported file.

sections.name: SCAN_TEMPLATE_ASSETS
sections.title: Template picture file names
sections.what: Lists the picture file names used for the logo, disclaimer, cover panel, findings bands, and cover photos. The names are plain file names inside the template folder.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps picture names in one place so they are not repeated across the slides.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a picture file without updating this list breaks the slide that uses it.

sections.name: INDUSTRY_PHOTOS
sections.title: Industry cover photo lookup
sections.what: Maps each industry key to a photo file for the cover slide. Dairy uses a cover photo instead. Industries without an entry get no photo.
sections.why: Likely reason: each industry gets a matching image on the cover.
sections.watch_out: A new industry needs an entry here, or its cover falls back to a plain grey background.

sections.name: Src
sections.title: Citation type alias
sections.what: Gives a short name to the citation type from the deck file, so the rest of this file can refer to it briefly.
sections.why: Likely reason: shorter code.

sections.name: r2
sections.title: Rounding helper
sections.what: Rounds a number to two decimal places so saved positions stay tidy.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps saved coordinates short and consistent.

sections.name: text
sections.title: Text box builder
sections.what: Creates a text element with default settings: Arial, 10 point, black, left aligned. Callers can override any of these.
sections.why: Likely reason: most slide text shares the same defaults, so each call needs fewer settings.
sections.watch_out: Font size is in points, not screen pixels, so a value copied from a screen measurement will look too large or small.

sections.name: rect
sections.title: Rectangle builder
sections.what: Creates a filled rectangle element at a given position and size.
sections.why: Likely reason: used for backgrounds, bands, and table cells.

sections.name: line
sections.title: Line builder
sections.what: Creates a line from a starting point with a given width and height. A negative width or height makes the line run the other way.
sections.why: Likely reason: one call draws both horizontal and vertical rules.
sections.watch_out: Negative lengths are easy to misread when moving a line, so check the direction after any change.

sections.name: ellipse
sections.title: Oval builder
sections.what: Creates an oval that fills the given box, used for chart bubbles and badges.
sections.why: Likely reason: bubbles and badges are drawn as ovals.

sections.name: image
sections.title: Picture builder
sections.what: Creates a picture element from a template picture file name at a given position and size.
sections.why: Likely reason: used for the cover, the logo, and decorative bands.
sections.watch_out: The picture name must match a real file in the template folder, or the picture will not appear.

sections.name: estimateLines
sections.title: Line count estimator
sections.what: Estimates how many lines a piece of text will take inside a given width, using average Arial character widths. Each paragraph break counts as a new line.
sections.why: Likely reason: the layout must size boxes before the text is drawn, and measuring real text is not possible here.
sections.watch_out: The estimate is rough, so real text may wrap differently and overflow a box slightly.

sections.name: textHeight
sections.title: Text height estimator
sections.what: Turns the estimated line count into a height in pixels, using a line spacing of 1.2.
sections.why: Likely reason: needed to stack text blocks one above another.
sections.watch_out: It shares the limits of the line count estimate.

sections.name: chunk
sections.title: List splitter
sections.what: Splits a list into groups of a given size. An empty list still returns one empty group.
sections.why: Likely reason: the glossary table splits projects into pages of a fixed number of rows.

sections.name: fmtMonthYear
sections.title: Month and year formatter
sections.what: Turns a date text into a month and year in English, such as a cover date. If the text is not a valid date, it returns the original text.
sections.why: Likely reason: the cover shows a readable month and year rather than a raw date.
sections.watch_out: The date is read as UTC, so the displayed month follows UTC.

sections.name: fmtMoney
sections.title: Money formatter
sections.what: Formats a money value for display. Large values get thousands separators with no decimals. Smaller values keep one decimal. Approximate values get a tilde in front. Missing values show n/a.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps budget figures short and readable in the table.
sections.watch_out: Values of 100 or more and values under 100 use different formats, so a column can look inconsistent.

sections.name: fmtYear
sections.title: Year formatter
sections.what: Keeps only the four-digit year from a date text. If none is found, it returns the original text, or n/a if the text is empty.
sections.why: Likely reason: the table shows only the planned year to save space.

sections.name: srcOf
sections.title: Project citation lookup
sections.what: Returns the citation stored for one project field, or nothing if there is none.
sections.why: Likely reason: each shown value can link to its evidence when a citation exists.
sections.watch_out: It can return nothing, so callers must handle the missing case.

sections.name: chrome
sections.title: Shared slide frame
sections.what: Builds the parts every content slide shares: the title, the red header rule, the grey footer rule, the disclaimer picture, the logo, and the page number. A title gets a citation if one is supplied, otherwise it is marked as editorial.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps every content slide visually consistent with the template.
sections.watch_out: The title is fixed at a set size and position, so a very long title can run into the rule below it.

sections.name: tag
sections.title: Corner category label
sections.what: Builds the uppercase label in the top right corner of a slide, such as Directional or Non exhaustive, with a short slanted line beside it.
sections.why: Likely reason: the template shows the slide's status in this corner.
sections.watch_out: The width is special-cased for the Non exhaustive label. A new label with a different length may need its own width.

sections.name: sourceLine
sections.title: Source note line
sections.what: Builds the small grey source note at the bottom of a slide.
sections.why: Likely reason: the template places the source and caveat line here.
sections.watch_out: The position is fixed, so a long note can overlap the footer.

sections.name: coverSlide, fade
sections.title: Cover slide and faded colour
sections.what: Builds the cover slide with its photos, panel, logo, title, and date. The photo layout depends on the industries present. A separate helper makes a faded colour for bubbles of projects still in delivery.
sections.why: Likely reason: the cover shows the industry, and faded colour signals that a forecast is not a final result.
sections.watch_out: The dairy-only photo layout is a special case. Other industries use the generic layout, so adding a new layout needs changes here.

sections.name: REGION_COLORS
sections.title: Region colours
sections.what: Gives each world region its colour for bubbles and the legend. The order of entries sets the order of the legend.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets readers tell regions apart by colour across all chart slides.
sections.watch_out: Region names must match exactly what the country lookup returns, or the colour is missing.

sections.name: COUNTRY_REGION
sections.title: Country to region patterns
sections.what: Lists text patterns for countries, each linked to a region. The patterns are checked in order and the first match wins.
sections.why: Likely reason: the source data has country names but no region, so names are matched to regions.
sections.watch_out: Order matters. A pattern placed too early can take countries that belong to a later region.

sections.name: regionOf
sections.title: Region lookup for countries
sections.what: Returns the region for a country name by checking the patterns in order. If nothing matches, it returns Europe.
sections.why: Likely reason: every project needs a colour, so a fallback is used.
sections.watch_out: The silent Europe fallback means an unrecognised country appears as European without any warning.

sections.name: PLOT
sections.title: Chart area dimensions
sections.what: Gives the edges of the chart area in pixels, measured from the template chart.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps all chart elements aligned with the template's plot frame.
sections.watch_out: Changing these numbers moves every chart element, so check the template after any edit.

sections.name: capacityOf
sections.title: Capacity value and unit
sections.what: Returns a capacity number and its unit. It uses the structured fields if they are valid. Otherwise it reads the number and unit from the display text, such as a value with a unit word after it. Invalid values return nothing.
sections.why: Likely reason: older saved decks have only the display text, so the number must be read from it.
sections.watch_out: Reading the number from text can misread ranges or unusual formats, which then appear as a wrong size.

sections.name: capexOf
sections.title: Budget used for sizing
sections.what: Returns the latest reported budget in millions if it is known, otherwise the planned budget. Returns nothing if neither is a positive number.
sections.why: Likely reason: the latest figure is preferred because it is the most recent known value.
sections.watch_out: This mixes planned and actual budgets. The chart labels say which one is shown, so readers should check that label.

sections.name: BubbleSizing
sections.title: Bubble sizing result shape
sections.what: Describes the result of sizing bubbles: the sizing rule used, the size for each project, the unit, the largest value, the number of projects with no size, and a note for the reader.
sections.why: Likely reason: the chart needs all of these to draw bubbles and explain them.
sections.watch_out: A missing size is stored as nothing, not zero. Code must not treat a missing size as a small bubble.

sections.name: bubbleSizing, ChartCoverageReason
sections.title: Bubble size calculation
sections.what: Works out each project's bubble size. Equal sizing gives every project the same value. Capacity sizing is used only when the projects share one dominant unit, and other units are left unsized. Budget sizing uses the latest reported budget. Bubble area is made proportional to the value.
sections.why: Likely reason: capacity in mixed units cannot be compared on one scale, so those projects are shown as unsized rather than mixed.
sections.watch_out: Projects in other units are left out of the size scale without being removed from the chart. The coverage note is the only sign of this.

sections.name: ChartCoverage, QUOTE_UNCONFIRMED, quoteUnconfirmed, finite
sections.title: Coverage result shape and helpers
sections.what: Defines the shape of the coverage result, which counts plotted projects and lists reasons for projects not plotted. Also defines helpers that check whether a budget quote is unconfirmed and whether a number is usable.
sections.why: Likely reason: the chart must explain its gaps openly, and these helpers keep that check in one place.
sections.watch_out: The unconfirmed check depends on exact check values, so a new check label must be added here to be recognised.

sections.name: chartCoverage
sections.title: Chart coverage summary
sections.what: Counts how many projects appear on each chart and groups the missing ones by reason, such as missing budget, missing schedule, unit mismatch, or unconfirmed quote. It also writes one sentence summarising this.
sections.why: Likely reason: readers must see why projects are missing rather than assuming the chart shows everything.
sections.watch_out: In the delivery view, one project can appear under more than one reason, so the reason counts can add up to more than the missing total.

sections.name: coverageBox
sections.title: Missing data explanation box
sections.what: Draws a small box that explains why few or no projects are plotted. It is placed in the first corner of the chart that does not cover a bubble or label.
sections.why: Likely reason: a near-empty chart should explain itself rather than look broken.
sections.watch_out: The height is estimated, and only bubbles and labels are checked as obstacles, so the box can cover other chart lines.

sections.name: chartSlide (part 1)
sections.title: Cost versus schedule chart axes
sections.what: Builds the cost versus schedule chart slide: header, corner label, and the axis scales worked out from the data with padding. It also sets up the four coloured quadrants split at the average cost and schedule values.
sections.why: Likely reason: axes that fit the data keep bubbles on the page, and the quadrants show which projects are above or below average.
sections.watch_out: The quadrant split uses the average, not the median, so one extreme project can move the split line.

sections.name: chartSlide: for
sections.title: Chart averages and region legend
sections.what: Writes the tick labels and axis titles, the average values with their formulas and citations, the project count, and the region legend showing only regions present in the data.
sections.why: Likely reason: readers need the averages and the number of projects to judge the chart.
sections.watch_out: Averages are shown with one decimal, so very close values can look different from the exact figures.

sections.name: chartSlide: for
sections.title: Chart bubbles and quadrant captions
sections.what: Places the four quadrant captions in free space, then draws each project as a bubble with its citation and size note. Projects still in delivery are drawn faded. In dense charts, only anchors and the most extreme projects get labels.
sections.why: Likely reason: captions and bubbles are placed first so text does not hide the data points.
sections.watch_out: In dense charts, many projects have no visible label. They are still clickable, so their names are only found by clicking or in the notes.

sections.name: chartSlide: for
sections.title: Chart project labels and footer
sections.what: Tries positions beside each bubble for the project's short name, and draws a leader line when the label has to move far. If no position is free, the label is dropped. If the chart has few points, it adds the coverage box. Finally it writes the source note with the count, the rules, and the caveat.
sections.why: Likely reason: labels that overlap are hard to read, so a crowded label is left out instead of drawn on top of another.
sections.watch_out: A dropped label is not reported on the slide. Full names are only in the interactive view and the notes.

sections.name: portfolioSlide (part 1)
sections.title: Portfolio scale chart
sections.what: Builds the portfolio chart of reported capacity against latest reported budget, using only projects that have both values in one comparable unit. It rounds the axis maxima up to tidy numbers and labels the five largest budgets.
sections.why: Likely reason: a separate chart stops capacity and budget from being read as delivery performance.
sections.watch_out: Projects with no comparable capacity unit are missing from this chart, so the total can be much smaller than the project count.

sections.name: portfolioSlide (part 2)
sections.title: Portfolio slide return
sections.what: Returns the finished portfolio slide with its layout name and title.
sections.why: Likely reason: the caller needs a slide object with the same shape as the others.

sections.name: buildScanChartSlide, Bullet, Cat
sections.title: Chart slide entry point
sections.what: Public entry point for chart slides. It returns the portfolio chart when that view is chosen, otherwise the cost versus schedule chart. The delivery path passes a fixed title and blank findings text, which the chart does not use.
sections.why: Likely reason: one function serves the interactive view, saved slides, and the export.
sections.watch_out: The delivery path fills in placeholder text that is not shown. Changing the chart's required inputs can break this path silently.

sections.name: bulletBlock
sections.title: Findings column text block
sections.what: Draws one column of findings. Each item shows a bold project name followed by its text. Long text is shortened with an ellipsis to fit the space, and the column stops when it runs out of room, but always shows at least the first item. Each claim is marked with its citations or as missing support.
sections.why: Likely reason: the summary slide must fit on one page and never run into the footer.
sections.watch_out: Shortening can cut the meaning of a sentence. Full reasons are kept in the appendix.

sections.name: bulletsFit
sections.title: Findings fit counter
sections.what: Counts how many findings fit in a given height, using the same spacing as the column drawing.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the layout decide how many findings to put on a page before drawing.
sections.watch_out: It must match the spacing in the column drawing, or findings will overflow the space.

sections.name: strapline
sections.title: Findings arrow footer line
sections.what: Draws the red arrow and centred caption at the bottom of a findings slide, under the negative or positive column.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed visual cue in the template that labels each side.
sections.watch_out: Its positions are fixed to the template, so moving a column means moving this line too.

sections.name: synthesisSlides, GLOSS_COLS
sections.title: Synthesis findings slides
sections.what: Builds the findings slides. It puts up to two negative findings and one positive finding on each page, and makes extra pages when there are more findings than fit. The column widths for the table are set in a separate list in the same section.
sections.why: Likely reason: one finding per column keeps each claim readable, and extra pages stop findings from being dropped.
sections.watch_out: The page count is set by the longer list, so one side can show empty space on the last page. The findings are labelled as directional, not proof of cause.

sections.name: glossarySlides (part 1)
sections.title: Project table pages
sections.what: Builds the project table pages. Each page holds up to eight projects, with headers for name, location, status, capacity, budget, and schedule end. Row heights grow with the text, and a footnote explains the implied end date.
sections.why: Likely reason: a full project list is kept in the deck, split across pages so each stays readable.
sections.watch_out: Long names or values make rows taller, and the table can then run into the footnote area.

sections.name: glossarySlides (part 2)
sections.title: Table page return
sections.what: Returns each table page with its id, layout name, title, and page number. Titles are numbered only when there is more than one page.
sections.why: Likely reason: the caller needs one slide object per page.
sections.watch_out: The source note text is cut to 300 characters, so the end of the caveat may be lost.

sections.name: appendixDivider
sections.title: Appendix divider slide
sections.what: Builds the black appendix divider with the word Appendix in white, two red rules, and a red paperclip drawn from straight segments.
sections.why: Likely reason: copies the template's divider so the appendix is visually separated.
sections.watch_out: The paperclip is made from a fixed list of points. It is decorative, so editing those points only changes the look.

sections.name: delayType
sections.title: Delay type label
sections.what: Labels a project as Cost and Schedule, Cost, Schedule, On budget or on time, or Incomplete figures. The labels say which overruns are above zero.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the reasons table group projects by what went over.
sections.watch_out: Zero or negative values count as not over, and a project is marked incomplete only when a value is entirely missing.

sections.name: reasonsSlides (part 1)
sections.title: Reason pages for the appendix
sections.what: Builds the appendix table of projects with their schedule and cost reasons. The table is split into several pages by row count and by height. Blank or unavailable reasons show a plain placeholder, and the phrase no cause stated in public sources is rewritten to cause not recorded in this snapshot.
sections.why: Likely reason: long tables must stay readable, and empty cells would look like errors.
sections.watch_out: The row limit comes from REASONS_MAX_ROWS, which is defined outside the reviewed code. The page height is a fixed number, so estimated text heights that are too small will cause overflow.

sections.name: reasonsSlides (part 2)
sections.title: Closing section heading
sections.what: Only a comment that marks the start of the closing section. It does nothing when the code runs.
sections.why: A label for readers of the file.

sections.name: thanksSlide
sections.title: Closing thank-you slide
sections.what: Builds a black slide with THANK YOU in white, centred, and a short white rule with a red accent beneath it.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the deck's visual style.
sections.watch_out: Positions are fixed to the 1280 by 720 canvas. A different canvas size would move the text off centre.

sections.name: makeScanSlides
sections.title: Assembling the full deck
sections.what: Chooses the appendix projects: those with both cost and schedule figures, plus those named in the synthesis. It then builds the cover, the chart, and the synthesis slides. If there are supporting projects, it adds the glossary, the appendix divider, and the reason pages. The deck always ends with the thank-you slide.
sections.why: Keeps the appendix to projects the story relies on or that have verifiable figures.
sections.watch_out: Projects are matched by trimmed, lower-case name, so two different projects with the same name will be treated as one.

sections.name: textVAlign
sections.title: Vertical text alignment rule
sections.what: Decides whether a text box is anchored to the top or the middle. Tall boxes that hold more than about 2.6 lines of text are top-anchored, unless their id ends with a label word such as title, name, or type.
sections.why: Keeps short labels centred while letting long body text start at the top.
sections.watch_out: The behaviour depends on how element ids are named. A new id that matches the pattern changes its alignment.

sections.name: parseColor
sections.title: Colour parser for export
sections.what: Turns a hex colour or an rgba colour into a six-digit hex value and a separate opacity number. It returns nothing for unrecognised input.
sections.why: The PowerPoint export needs the colour and the transparency as separate values.
sections.watch_out: Eight-digit hex colours are cut to six digits, so their transparency is lost. Short three-digit hex codes are expanded before use.

sections.name: ptToPx
sections.title: Points to pixels conversion
sections.what: Converts a size in points to pixels by multiplying by four thirds.
sections.why: Font sizes are stored in points but drawn in pixels on the 1280 by 720 canvas.
sections.watch_out: This assumes the standard relation between points and pixels. A different scale would need this changed.

sections.name: sceneKit
sections.title: Reusable building blocks for other decks
sections.what: Exports a bundle of drawing helpers, the font, the red accent colour, the appendix divider, the thank-you slide, and a cover maker. The cover maker takes a title and a list of industries and builds a cover from them.
sections.why: Lets another tool such as Lessons Learnt match this deck's look without copying the code.
sections.watch_out: The cover maker passes a fake scan input with a cast, so it only supplies the fields the cover needs. Making the cover read more fields would break callers without any error at compile time.

summary: Builds the slide layout for the Reality Scan presentation, from cover to closing slide, and provides drawing building blocks that other decks can reuse.
purpose: Turns a finalized scan into a list of slides, each with positioned text, boxes, lines, and images, so the app can show or export the deck.
why: The header says the output is pure and deterministic, so the same scan always gives the same deck. Likely reason: saved and compared decks must not drift between runs.
how: makeScanSlides picks which projects go in the appendix. It then builds the cover and the chart slide, adds synthesis slides, and when there are supporting projects, adds glossary pages, an appendix divider, and reason pages. It finishes with a thank-you slide. The earlier parts of this file, which are not all shown here, define the drawing helpers and the chart and table layouts. The later helpers convert colours and point sizes and decide vertical text alignment for both renderers.
inputs: A finalized scan containing projects, a synthesis of positive and negative findings, and cover details.
outputs: A list of slides. Each slide has an id, a layout name, a title, and a set of positioned elements. The colour and size helpers return plain values, and sceneKit exposes the building blocks.
risks: The layout is fixed to a 1280 by 720 canvas, so text changes can overflow. Text heights are estimated, which may not match the real renderer. A project left out of the appendix is intentional when it has no complete figures and is not cited.
debug: If a slide is missing, check the conditions in makeScanSlides, especially the appendix condition and the cited names. If text overlaps or is cut off, check the height estimates and the vertical alignment rule. If colours look wrong, check the input format passed to parseColor.
